title: Central Texas Brisket
summary: Salt, pepper, post oak, and patience. The packer is the whole argument.
ingredients: Optional: a dust of granulated garlic
method: Trim hard fat off the point, square the edges, leave a 1/4-inch fat cap on the flat.
Season heavy the night before. Equal parts salt and pepper is the religion.
Smoke fat-cap down until the bark sets and the flat hits about 165°F.
Wrap in peach paper when the bark does not smear. Return to the pit.
Pull when a probe slides like warm butter, usually 200–205°F in the thickest flat.
Rest in a dry cooler at least 2 hours. Slice the flat against the grain. Cube or chop the point.
note: If the smoke is white and thick, you are burning fuel, not cooking beef.

title: Santa Maria Tri-Tip
summary: Live oak, a hard sear, and a medium-rare center. California pit beef.
ingredients: Santa Maria seasoning: salt, black pepper, garlic, parsley
A little oil to tack the rub
method: Season all sides an hour ahead.
Sear hard over the coals until crusted.
Move off direct heat and cook to 125–130°F internal for medium-rare.
Rest 15 minutes. Slice thin against the grain — this cut changes direction mid-roast.
note: Serve with pinquito beans and salsa, not a sticky bottle sauce.
